At a repeated product eigenvalue, summands have distinct first-factor eigenvalues; consecutive fiber restrictions form a nonzero Vandermonde matrix. PBH gives sharp coordinate-input cardinality. On a square grid, n-1 paired modes yield eigenvalue 4 at coupling t=1; a hypothetical multiplicity-n sum at any t>0 forces the order-reversed pairing, then t=1 and contradiction 4 cos(pi/n)(cos(pi/n)-1)<0. The included exact Fraction Kalman-rank verifier passed 25 cases. No numerical experiment replaces the proof.

value.rationale: A precise coordinate-actuator optimization and explicit always-attaining pattern are established for a natural broad class of product networks, including every eigenvalue collision and every positive factor coupling. The additional all-coupling square-grid budget n-1 is genuinely sharper than using a full boundary line, and requires a spectral obstruction proof beyond the usual lower-bound multiplicity at one chosen coupling. The theorem discriminates one-parameter robustness from arbitrary edge-weight robustness. No unproved sensitivity or energy bound is claimed.
